title: fix(agents): model catalog worker crashes leave no trace in logs or status
body:
Closes #161738

Related: #157989, #158738, #161280, #159514, #160544, #155753, #161379. Same code, different fixes: #159935, #161125, #159448, #161456.

## What Problem This Solves

Fixes: the Gateway's model-catalog worker can fail over and over (for example `ERR_WORKER_OUT_OF_MEMORY` at its 512 MB heap limit) with nothing in the log and no failure shown in `status`, even though every failure republishes all borrowing agent catalogs.

## User Impact

Operators now get one warning per failed catalog worker, with the worker's reason (out of memory, exit code, or timeout) and the number of agent catalogs to republish on a new worker. `status` gains `workerPools.modelCatalog.workerFailures`, and the startup `memory.ready` trace gains `modelCatalogWorkerFailures`, both counting failures since the Gateway started. A worker that exits while idle is counted and logged when it exits; the next catalog request replaces it.

No config, stored data, migration, or recovery behavior changes. Shutdown, plugin retirement and pool rotation are not counted or logged.

## Why This Change Was Made

Background renewals drop their rejection, and a failed pool is replaced by one whose `getSnapshot()` starts again at `workersCreated: 1`. So a worker that died every few minutes looked like a healthy one. On 2026.9.6 about 90 silent worker deaths in a day went unnoticed until filesystem monitoring caught the capture folders turning over (details in #161738).

With crash restart off, a catalog pool closes itself when its worker fails, exits or times out, even if no request is waiting. Catalog pools are now a small internal `WorkerTaskPool` subclass that reports its first close to the pool owner (`getGatewayCatalogPool`); no plugin SDK option changes. When the pool closed itself, the owner counts the failure and logs the reason right then; recovery still republishes the affected catalogs with the next request. A pool its owner closes (shutdown, plugin retirement, rotation) is marked `closing` first, so those closes are not reported. The counter lives on the existing global pool singleton, so it survives pool replacement. Pool construction and the worker-data type moved to `prepared-model-catalog-worker.pool.ts` with the subclass, which keeps `prepared-model-catalog-worker.ts` under its 700-line cap (677 counted lines, was 700). `docs/logging.md` and `docs/plugins/architecture.md` describe the new field and warning.

## Evidence

- Regression: the updated `src/agents/prepared-model-catalog-worker.pool.integration.test.ts` fails 3 of 3 changed tests against the original code (missing `workerFailures`).
- Idle exit (after the second review): the test "logs and counts an idle catalog worker exit before a request recovers it" settles every catalog (`activeTasks: 0`, `pendingTasks: 0`), terminates the worker, and sees `workerFailures` + 1 and one `... worker exited with code 1` warning before any request arrives; the next request recovers without counting or logging it again. On 5a1a51e that point had no warning yet (its version of this test asserted so and passed in CI), so the new assertion fails there.
- Guard check: with only `current.closing = true` removed, "does not report renewal failure during warm shutdown" fails (the shutdown is counted as a failure). The retirement case is guarded by the retirement signal and still passes.
- First two commits, on f3672acef: `node scripts/run-vitest.mjs src/agents/prepared-model-catalog-worker.pool.integration.test.ts --maxWorkers=1` passes 13/13 (1 m 49 s wall for the first 12 on an idle host; 2 m 35 s to 3 m 4 s for 13 on a heavily loaded host, including worker compile).
  - A terminated worker produces exactly one `model catalog worker failed; N agent catalog(s) will be republished on a new worker (failure N since start): ... worker exited with code 1` (wording as of 47c2052) warning and `workerFailures` + 1, while the replacement pool reports `workersCreated: 1`.
  - Warm shutdown and warm plugin retirement leave `workerFailures` unchanged and log no warning.
- Siblings pass (8 files, 30 tests, 3 shards, 117 s): catalog-worker unit, captures, retirement, directory, reuse and workspace-heap integration, `server-close.model-acquisition`, and `health.owner-routing`. The last one needed its exact `workerPools` expectation updated.
- `tsgo` core and all 27 core test shards pass. `oxfmt --check`, `oxlint`, docs formatting and markdownlint are clean on the changed files; the line-cap ratchet passes.
- Test cost: one new integration test (5.3 s to 5.8 s locally; it reuses the file's fleet fixture and the existing `loadCompletedFullCatalog` helper, with no new timers or worker pins). Three existing tests gain assertions with unchanged per-test time (the failure test took 5.9 s before and 5.4 s after on the same host; the shutdown and retirement tests take 3.6 s each).
- Not covered: a real `ERR_WORKER_OUT_OF_MEMORY` in a test (too slow for per-PR CI). The test terminates the worker instead, which goes through the same pool-failure path; the OOM text reaches the warning through the same error message.
- 47c2052 (warn at exit) was checked in CI, not in a local run ([CI run](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/36721237350)): `prepared-model-catalog-worker.pool.integration.test.ts` passes 13/13 in [`checks-node-changed-compact-large-5-2`](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/36721237350/job/109907200101) (idle-exit test 7.0 s in CI, 5.7 s on the previous head; no new test), and no catalog-worker test failed in any shard. The lint, type, guard, boundary, docs and build jobs pass. Before pushing, `oxfmt --check` and `oxlint` with the repository configs were clean on the changed files.
- CI failures on 47c2052 are in tests that do not import the catalog worker: `server-runtime-subscriptions.shutdown.test.ts` (also failing on unrelated PRs today, e.g. [#157641](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/36708976472/job/109866442398)), `code-mode-node.watchdog.test.ts` (Bun lane), `update-cli.target-schema.test.ts`, and `workspace-result-repository.test.ts` (`ENOENT` on a temporary repository's `.git/objects/maintenance.lock`; it passed on 5a1a51e). On 5a1a51e the only failures were `server-runtime-subscriptions.shutdown.test.ts` and `session-activity-summaries.test.ts`, which also fails on `main` ([scheduled run](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/36697144647/job/109828001081)).

## Maintainer runtime verification (2026-10-07)

Verified unchanged head `36bf1186fe284b1910f3287a083a899d078a2b6e` against main `7b66485dcd9b04672d5b44d74d6aee000b6f0e7e` in isolated Docker:

- Built Gateway, two configured agents, real provider fixture exiting the catalog worker with code 23. Main logs no catalog-failure warning and exposes no `workerFailures`. This head logs exactly one warning per failed worker, including exit code 23 and affected-agent counts (2 on the first failure, 1 after recovery); `gateway call status` reports lifetime counts 0 → 1 → 2. The healthy worker emits no failure warning. Both versions recover through the existing next-request path; no recovery policy was changed.
- The PR catalog tests on main fail 4/13 cases for the missing diagnostic field; this head passes 13/13 (132.37 s wrapper, 113.08 s Vitest). Health owner-routing and Gateway agent tests pass 405/405 on this head. The added health expectations fail on main for the missing field.
- Candidate full build completed; core `pnpm tsgo` ran without diagnostics. The main build produced the runtime artifacts used above but its wrapper reported `EPROCESSGROUP_CLEANUP_FAILED` after SDK-export verification. Runtime fixtures use tmpfs because the initial overlay-filesystem fixture encountered `EBADF`.
- One real `gpt-5-mini` call through the built `agent exec` command, reasoning low and output budget 4096, returned `P161740_LIVE_OK` (one assistant turn). Temporary credentials were removed.
- [Exact-head CI](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/37437933038) has one failed execution job: [`checks-node-changed-compact-small-1`](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/37437933038/job/112184889916), where `agent.test.ts` was killed following a SQLite WAL sidecar identity mismatch in the `openclaw-gateway-terminal-main-newer` fixture. The same test file passes all 392 cases both at this head and with this PR's production catalog changes reverted. Its `agent.mocks.test-utils.ts:191-214` stubs model-runtime acquisition; these logging/snapshot changes cannot change SQLite WAL identity enforcement or temporary-store teardown. The two red `openclaw/ci-gate` surfaces aggregate that failure. Cancelled jobs: 0. `security-fast` is green in this run.
- [ClawSweeper is ready on this exact head](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/pull/161740#issuecomment-5906837247), with no blocking correctness finding.

Overlap checked: #159935 is closed without merge; #159448 merged on October 4 and current main merges cleanly here. #161125 remains open and its heap-recycling change will need to adapt to the moved heap-limit/pool construction. #161456 remains an open integration draft with overlapping catalog/source-capture preparation. Neither is a replacement for these diagnostics.

No overlap with Pash/Sarah changes. Thanks to @matthematics1137 for both the report and the fix. No source changes or replacement commits were needed for this verification.
